newsitem.title: UK: Germanium metal trade ponders Ukrainian tender.
newsitem.headline: Germanium metal trade ponders Ukrainian tender.

text.p: Strong market talk that a Ukrainian germanium metal tender has recently been concluded has left Western traders nervous of further price gyrations over the coming weeks, some dealers said on Tuesday.
Traders said they believed 6-1/2 tonnes of stockpiled Ukrainian material was sold at the tender, but they were unable to give a firm indication of what price level the transaction was concluded at.
Germanium metal is quoted at around $1,850/$1,950 a kilo, having peaked this year at $1,925/$2,075 in mid-June against a backdrop of Japanese demand and tight supplies.
Referring to the tender one trader commented, "The price was below the lower end of market expectations."
He believed that three companies had purchased the material.

Germanium is a by-product of zinc and copper ores, extracted in refining. It is used in high-frequency and high-power electronic applications, such as infra-red systems, fibre optics and semi-conductors.
Opinions remained divided on what impact the tender would have to the germanium market as a whole.
Several argued that the sale had already been factored into the market and that 6-1/2 tonnes could be absorbed by the booming fibre optics industry.
"It can be absorbed as long as it is handled correctly," one trader said.
Traders said the material was likely to sold on to the market between the middle and end of September.
Some traders remained wary of the emergence of the material.
"It is likely to cause a shock wave and may tempt longs to liquidate further," one trader said.
Supply/demand figures are hard to pin down as germanium remains an opaque market, but according to one source demand in 1996 could be above 90 tonnes, while supply was near 80 tonnes.
In 1995 supply was around 52 tonnes, while demand stood close to 80 tonnes, the same source said.
